source_assessment.notes: SRC-001 is an official Showakan chronology page but is retrospective; its declared source_type=reliable_secondary_or_research is appropriate for the current record.

evidence_integrity.notes: EVD-001 through EVD-004 are marked as paraphrases and stay within statements present on SRC-001; no quotation/paraphrase mismatch was found.

source_evidence_support.notes: The Showakan 1973 section supports the 11/22 Tama City sold-out notice, word-of-mouth shortage rumor, hoarding, oil-price/inflation context, economic panic, and a 2020 SNS comparison.

primary_source_relation.notes: SRC-001 is a retrospective chronology and the current metadata does not identify the primary record from which it directly derives; direct_derivative is therefore not independently established by the record.

earliest_attestation.notes: The artifact uses the 1973 material as an event/history anchor and does not claim that the 11/22 sold-out notice identifies the first utterance or first transmission of the rumor.

uncertainty_preservation.notes: EVD-004 is explicitly marked as a later comparison outside the 1973 scope; the artifact does not convert the documented 1973 event into a claim about an identified originator.

salient_evidence_completeness.notes: SRC-001 gives salient detail for the 2020 comparison—COVID-19 context and the specific false claim that toilet paper was manufactured/imported from China—but EVD-004 reduces this to a generic shortage misinformation statement. This detail matters because the downstream VAR-002 uses manufacturing/import anxiety to distinguish the later variant.

findings.summary: SRC-001 is labeled direct_derivative without an identified direct primary-source chain.
findings.rationale: The source is a later Showakan chronology. Neither the locator nor bibliographic metadata identifies a primary record that SRC-001 directly reproduces or derives from, so the stronger relation label is not demonstrable from the current artifact.
findings.impact: The historical content remains usable as a reliable secondary source, but the provenance relation is stated more strongly than the stored metadata supports.
findings.fix_direction: Change relation_to_primary to unknown or document the specific primary source/record that establishes a direct derivative relationship.

findings.summary: EVD-004 omits the specific 2020 misinformation premise and COVID-19 context present in SRC-001.
findings.rationale: SRC-001 states that in February 2020, during the global COVID-19 outbreak, misinformation claimed toilet paper would become scarce because it was manufactured/imported from China; EVD-004 records only a generic shortage misinformation spread on SNS and hoarding.
findings.impact: The Evidence layer does not contain all salient meaning used to distinguish the later 2020 comparison, and downstream VAR-002 currently contains details not represented in Evidence.
findings.fix_direction: Expand EVD-004 (or add a separate Evidence item) to preserve the COVID-19 context and manufacturing/import claim if VAR-002 is retained; otherwise remove those unsupported downstream details.

review_notes: Independent semantic review of the fixed 0363/00 target. The core 1973 evidence is supported; findings concern provenance strength and completeness of the scope-external 2020 comparison.
